about: The sibling types the bakes cover (LS-086, D-116: 'all siblings but try to match as much as possible'): each (type, airline) seen at SFO that the fleet library lacks, baked from the airline's library type closest in length and generation. tools/fleet/bake.mjs maps it by station, anchored at the nose and the tail, and skips any pair the library has exactly. 15 Nov: the rest of the library converted, so United's A319, 737-700, 737-900 and 777-200, Alaska's and Delta's 737-900, Delta's A319, Southwest's 737-700 and China Airlines' 777F are exact now and left this list; United's E170 and Aer Lingus's A330-300 joined it. Source: docs/research/fleet-gaps.md. 15 Nov (kit v0.7 and the freighter rule): FedEx's 777F and MD-11F from its 767-300F (the same livery; the 777F onto the kit's b777f, as the server draws a cargo operator's B77L, the MD-11F onto md11), and United Express's and American Eagle's ERJ-145s (CommuteAir, Piedmont) from the airlines' E175s. 15 Nov (the traced row, main): Cathay's A350-900 from its 777-300ER, Air New Zealand's 777-300ER from its 787-9, Lufthansa's A380 from its A350-900. 16 Nov (the other regions: "why don't JFK's aircrafts have hifi liveries?", main's snapshot mix at JFK, LGA, EWR and SEA): JetBlue's A320 from its A321, American's A319 from its A320, United's 787-10 from its 787-9, Alaska's 737-700 from its 737-800. 16 Nov, morning (the snapshots’ new pairs at LGA and EWR): Air Canada’s A320 from its A321, American’s and Delta’s E170s from their E175s, and Delta Connection’s CRJ-900 from Delta’s E175 (the same Delta Connection livery: Endeavor’s CRJs, 7 seen at JFK and LGA). (United Express’s CRJ-700 isn’t baked: the kit draws a CRJ-700 as its CRJ-900 scaled, a stand-in, and stand-ins get none; the painter dresses it.) And Air Canada Express’s E175 (E75S: the kit’s e175) from its CRJ-900 (the same Air Canada Express livery).
